rule: Answer 5 (Samuel, 2026-09-25): a figure no existing visual type can draw gets a native figure or widget type, never a static book image. This file is that build's spec: every figure reference typed once, each type covered by a kind that exists or named as a gap with the kind to build.

number_line.label: Number line, interval or inequality on a line

cartesian_points.label: Points, segments and polygons on the Cartesian plane

examples.evidence: 'plot the following points' in question stem

straight_line_graph.label: Straight-line graph(s)
straight_line_graph.limits: function_graph draws one line; two or more lines on one set of axes (simultaneous equations) are drawn as coordinate_plot segments.

examples.evidence: 'same set of axes' in words before; chapter 'Equations and inequalities' graphs lines

right_triangle_trig.label: One right-angled triangle for a trigonometric ratio
right_triangle_trig.limits: trig_triangle draws ONE right triangle and its angleDeg is 30|45|60|θ: a printed 17° is drawn as θ with the value in the caption. A real-world backdrop (building, ladder, escalator) is not drawn.

examples.evidence: 'triangle' in the words just before; 'right-angled' in the words just before

circle_diagram.label: Circle with centre and radius (area, circumference)

mapping_diagram.label: Mapping diagram / function machine (inputs to outputs)
mapping_diagram.limits: A function machine's rule box becomes the caption.

sample_space_diagram.label: Sample space: outcome grid, dice or coin outcomes
sample_space_diagram.limits: Dice faces and coins are drawn as labels, not pictures.

dot_plot.label: Dot plot of a data set

line_chart.label: Line chart of data (relative frequency against trials)
line_chart.limits: Drawn as points joined by segments, with a dashed reference line as a segment.

gap.why: function_graph draws linear and quadratic only; a hyperbola is two branches either side of dashed asymptotes, sampled so it never joins across x = 0.
One more fn value on the hyperbola's sampler and asymptote: one branch, one horizontal asymptote.

trig_graph.label: Sine, cosine or tangent graph over 0°–360°

gap.why: A degree axis 0°–360° with 90° ticks, amplitude and period, and tan's vertical asymptotes; none of this exists in function_graph.

multi_function_graph.label: Two or more curves on one set of axes (intersections, match-the-graph)

gap.why: function_graph takes one fn; these figures need several labelled curves, possibly of different families, with their intersection points marked.

cartesian_trig_angle.label: Angle in standard position on the Cartesian plane (5.8)

gap.proposed_kind: coordinate_plot (extended): angle arc from +x axis, reference triangle, quadrant labels
gap.why: coordinate_plot has points and segments but no angle arc from the positive x-axis, no dashed drop to the axis and no quadrant (CAST) labels.

lines_and_angles.label: Lines and angles: parallel lines, transversals, angle pairs

gap.why: geo_scene is circle-centred and has no parallel arrows or equal-angle marks; a transversal figure is all parallel arrows and angle arcs.

examples.evidence: no words of its own; sibling ref 745 (b04088) is lines_and_angles by euclid:lines_and_angles-weak

triangle_geometry.label: Triangle geometry: classification, congruency, similarity, Pythagoras

gap.why: geo_scene can place segments and angles but not equal-length ticks, right-angle squares or dashed construction lines, which carry the argument in a congruency or similarity figure.

quadrilateral_geometry.label: Quadrilaterals and polygons: properties, proofs, naming

gap.why: Needs parallel arrows, equal-side ticks, diagonals and numbered angles; none is in geo_scene.
A triangle with its mid-points marked by ticks and the joining segment marked parallel: the same marks geometry_diagram adds.

trig_composite_diagram.label: Trigonometry on a composite figure (two triangles, rhombus, trapezium)

gap.why: trig_triangle draws one right triangle; these share sides between triangles or sit inside a quadrilateral.

plane_shape_measure.label: Plane shape with labelled dimensions (area, perimeter)

gap.why: Dimension labels on sides and a dashed perpendicular height; no kind draws a labelled polygon today.

solid_3d.label: 3-D solid: prism, cylinder, pyramid, cone, sphere

gap.why: No kind draws in 3-D: an oblique projection with hidden edges dashed, labelled dimensions, on iPad Safari with keyboard operation.

solid_net.label: Net of a solid (the solid unfolded)

gap.why: A net is flat faces laid out edge to edge; it shares the solid's model, and the fold animation is what makes it teach.

venn_diagram.label: Venn diagram of sets or events

gap.why: Two or three overlapping sets in a sample-space frame, with counts or elements per region and a shaded region; no kind draws sets.
stat_chart's bars have gaps and categorical labels; a histogram is contiguous bars over class intervals on a numeric axis.
Five markers on a number line joined as box and whiskers; small, but no kind has it.

pattern_sequence.label: Picture pattern growing term by term (matchsticks, tiles, dots)

gap.why: A motif repeated by a growth rule, term 1, 2, 3, …; nothing draws a picture sequence, and a generated one must match the rule exactly.

annotated_expression.label: Expression with labelled arrows (expanding, base and exponent)

gap.why: Typeset maths with curved arrows and labels pointing at its parts.
